title: Calvin in Geneva
hookLine: a shy French lawyer builds a church, schools and a refugee city

lines: A SHY MAN WHO LOVED THE SHADOWS.
STAY, OR GOD WILL CURSE YOUR STUDIES.
cards: One night's stop. That was the plan. A young Frenchman trained in law, who has had to leave his own country over his faith, is passing through Geneva on his way somewhere quiet, to read and write in peace.
He later calls himself shy by nature, someone who loved the shadows. But word gets around, and an older preacher named William Farel comes to find him. Stay and help, Farel says.
The young man says no. Then, Farel tells him, God will curse his quiet studies. The young man stays.

teach.b: We know about that night because Calvin told it himself, in the preface to his commentary on the Psalms. Farel's words terrified him, he says, as if God had reached down and stopped him on the road. Geneva wasn't easy.
The city threw him out once, later called him back, and he came. What he built there had three pieces.

teach.h: A CHURCH, WITH DEACONS FOR THE POOR.
teach.b: A church, organized with pastors, teachers, elders and deacons, the deacons charged with caring for the poor and the sick.
Schools, so children could read the Bible for themselves and young pastors could be trained. And a city of refuge.

Calvin knew what it was to be a refugee, and people fleeing for their faith came to Geneva from France and other lands, with funds set up to help the poor among them. The Bible gives that welcome deep roots.

teach.h: STRANGERS, AS ONE BORN AMONG YOU.
teach.b: In the King James wording of Leviticus: "the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt."
Geneva in Calvin's time was also strict and sometimes harsh, and it put people on trial for their beliefs. Historians still weigh that part, and it belongs in the story.
Churches in the Reformed and Presbyterian family trace themselves back to Geneva. And the shy man who wanted a quiet room spent the rest of his life in a busy, contested city full of strangers.

how: Reformed and Presbyterian churches trace their roots to Calvin's Geneva; their deacons and members often work with refugees and newcomers, and some congregations sponsor refugee families.

practice: Think of someone who had to leave home: a neighbor, a coworker, a family in the news, maybe someone in your own family tree.

What did they leave behind, and what would welcome look like for them: a meal, help for new arrivals, learning to say their name properly? If you pray, pray for them by name; if you don't, hold them in mind with care.

wordCard.voice: Calvin. The refugee lawyer, pressed to stay in Geneva, who built a church, schools and a city that took in people fleeing for their faith.
